# Windjammer

> Windjammer is a high-level language that compiles to Rust, with ownership and borrowing inferred by the compiler. The same `.wj` source also runs in an interpreter and has Go, JavaScript and WebAssembly backends of lower maturity.

Version 0.50.0 (pre-1.0: language and compiler behaviour can change between minor versions). You have probably seen almost no Windjammer in training data: do not guess from Rust or Python. Use `wj check --json FILE` for diagnostics, `wj run --interpret FILE` for an instant run, and `wj docs <terms>` for offline search. `llms-full.txt` contains the agent guide, CLI reference, backend matrix, keywords and MCP tool list inline.

## Start here

- [Windjammer for agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/agent/WINDJAMMER_FOR_AGENTS.md): The edit-check-run loop, core idioms and pitfalls; every code block is executed in CI
- [CLI reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/reference/cli.md): Every `wj` subcommand, generated from the clap definitions
- [Backend support matrix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/reference/targets.md): Which backends pass how much of the conformance corpus (generated)

## Language

- [Keywords and operators](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/reference/keywords.md): Lexer keywords (generated from the lexer)
- [Intrinsics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/reference/intrinsics.md): Built-in functions available on every backend
- [Standard library](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/reference/stdlib.md): Signatures scanned from `std/**/*.wj`
- [Error and lint codes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/reference/errors.md): WJ#### and W#### codes
- [Grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/windjammer.ebnf): EBNF cross-checked against the real parser
- [Ownership inference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/language-design/ownership-inference.md): What the compiler infers and how
- [Cheatsheet from Rust](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/agent/cheatsheet_from_rust.md): Rust to Windjammer mapping (also from Go, Python and TypeScript in the same directory)

## Project state

- [Known gaps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/known-gaps.md): The ranked, honest list of what is missing
- [Why Windjammer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/WHY.md): Comparisons with Rust, Go, Python, Zig, Mojo and Gleam; goals are labelled as goals
- [Roadmap](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/ROADMAP.md): Work with a concrete plan attached

## Optional

- [Interpreter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/INTERPRETER.md): What `wj run --interpret` supports and rejects (generated)
- [Architecture decision records](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/docs/adr/README.md): Open and accepted design decisions
- [agent-dx benchmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/bench/agent-dx/README.md): Same 60 tasks in six languages, graded by hidden tests
- [Performance benchmarks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffreyfriedman/windjammer/main/benchmarks/README.md): Inputs, runners and the last recorded results
